OURS claim: Server pseudonym-lookup cost grows linearly with the number of devices (O(N x W)), vs constant in Table V
verdict: PARTIAL: depends on guessed inputs (sensitivity, not evidence)
evidence (computed): OMNeT++ sensitivity runs (our model, BASE Table II, measured ESP8266 constants), mean latency N=100 -> N=1000: server resolves every device in range, 5% adversaries: 17.0 -> 1045 ms; same without adversaries 16.2 -> 227 ms; each server resolves only its own devices (14 -> 20 per server): 11.4 -> 17.5 ms; laptop-class server: 1.29 -> 1.86 ms; 800 m range: 5554 ms at N=1000. The independent SimPy model agrees (17.2 -> 683 ms, laptop 1.2 -> 1.8 ms, nearest-only 10.4 -> 16.6 ms). So the lookup cost scales with the number of devices a server must resolve, and whether that is 'all N' or ~20 depends on enrolment policy, server class and adversary load, none of which BASE specifies. OURS should state it as a conditional.
